data.title: AI extinction searches just spiked. Deutsche Bank says we've seen this movie before
data.description:
Bob Metcalfe was so sure the internet would collapse in 1996 that he later blended his wrong prediction into a smoothie and drank it. Three decades on, Deutsche Bank says the tech world's AI doom-calling deserves the same skepticism.

AI fears come in waves

Concerns about AI have moved in waves since ChatGPT's launch nearly four years ago. Google Trends data showed a spike in searches for "SaaSpocalypse" in February and “jobs apocalypse” in May, while searches for “AI extinction” have surged recently, Deutsche Bank said.

But the report noted that all three remain far behind searches for “AI bubble,” which itself trails "deepfake," "AI students," "AI risk," and, with the highest interest among the terms examined, "cybersecurity." Nearly all of those searches have increased this year, according to Google Trends data cited by Deutsche Bank.

The latest surge in concern comes after Evan Hubinger, Alignment Science Lead at Anthropic (ANTHRO), said AI could potentially cause catastrophic harm to humanity within the next decade, adding that Anthropic’s alignment work is lacking a clear solution for the risks posed by increasingly capable systems.

History is littered with bad technology forecasts

Deutsche Bank said technology predictions have a particularly mixed record, citing examples including IBM Chairman Thomas Watson's 1943 estimate of a global market for perhaps five computers and Elon Musk's repeated forecasts since 2013 for widespread adoption of self-driving cars.

The report also said predictions about AI that have not unfolded as expected. Geoffrey Hinton had said in 2016 that deep learning would outperform radiologists within five to 10 years. Instead, the number of radiologists increased about 10% over the following decade, with Deutsche Bank attributing the increase partly to AI's limitations and partly to rising healthcare demand.

OpenAI (OPENAI) CEO Sam Altman also revised an earlier prediction that AI could perform 30%-40% of economic tasks in the not-too-distant future. In May, he said his team had been roughly right about technological predictions but “pretty wrong” about their economic and social implications, according to Deutsche Bank.

The AI investment question

Deutsche Bank said predicting AI's future is not only about what the technology will eventually be capable of, but also when those capabilities will arrive and how quickly businesses will adopt them.

That uncertainty extends to the enormous investment underway. The report framed the question as whether more than $5T in investment by hyperscalers over the next five years will pay off before the advanced semiconductor chips being purchased become redundant. It also noted that asset prices are an even more uncertain derivative of changing expectations.

Deutsche Bank said the debate also includes competing views over whether AI could transform the economy, create new jobs, and solve problems such as energy and water consumption, while critics argue that attention to extinction scenarios can distract from more immediate issues such as deepfakes, copyright infringement, and cybersecurity failures.

AI may still deliver major gains

The report cautioned against assuming that failed predictions mean AI will not have a major impact. Deutsche Bank pointed to weather forecasting as an example of how AI can produce substantial gains even when the underlying improvement in predictive limits is relatively modest.

Deep-learning models extend the standard physics-based predictability horizon from about eight days to nine days but can generate state-of-the-art forecasts 100,000 times faster and 10,000 times more energy-efficiently, according to the report.

The report's broader conclusion was that the ultimate impact of AI will depend not only on what technology companies build but also on how businesses and consumers use it across the wider economy.

data.title: Enova shares fall as company withdraws Grasshopper acquisition applications
data.description:
Enova International (ENVA) shares fell ~18% in premarket trading on Tuesday after the company withdrew regulatory applications tied to its proposed acquisition of Grasshopper Bancorp. The company reaffirmed its 2026 guidance and said it intends to accelerate share repurchases

Throughout the application process, "Enova has worked constructively and transparently with regulators, responding promptly and fully to requests and building an application that Enova believes satisfies the statutory criteria for approval," the company said.

"After a thorough evaluation, we are confident that withdrawing our applications is the best decision for Enova and our shareholders."

Enova said bank regulatory guidelines and attitudes have not kept pace with the realities of meeting the credit needs of tens of millions of consumers and small businesses underserved by traditional banks.

"Regulators do not have clear standards for nonbanks that want to become banks and that serve customers whose credit needs today are met mostly outside of the banking system. Without clearly articulated standards, the process is susceptible to political pressure and outside advocacy, rather than being guided strictly by the statutory factors that should govern it," said Steve Cunningham, Enova's CEO.

data.title: Piedmont Realty Trust prices $200M notes offering
data.description:
Piedmont Realty Trust (PDM) said its operating partnership priced a private offering of $200M of 2.875% exchangeable senior notes due 2031.

The offering is expected to settle Sept. 17, subject to customary closing conditions. The initial purchasers also have an option to buy up to an additional $30M of notes.

The notes will pay 2.875% annual interest semiannually and mature Feb. 1, 2031, unless earlier exchanged, redeemed, or repurchased. The initial exchange price is $12.65 per Piedmont share, representing a premium of about 37.5% to the company’s Sept. 14 closing price of $9.20.

Piedmont expects net proceeds of about $194.3M, or approximately $223.5M if the additional notes are fully purchased. The company plans to use the proceeds, along with cash, borrowings, and proceeds from forward sale transactions, to redeem all outstanding 9.25% senior notes due 2028, including the applicable make-whole premium and accrued interest.

About $50M of the proceeds will also be used to repurchase 5.43M shares of Piedmont common stock from certain purchasers of the notes in privately negotiated transactions.

data.title: Biggest stock movers Tuesday: PLAY, ENVA, and more
data.description:
Stock futures inched lower Tuesday morning as Middle East supply risks, high bond yields, and calls for a deliberate pause in AI development weigh on sentiment ahead of the Fed rate decision.

Here are some of Tuesday's biggest stock movers:

Biggest stock gainers

  • Radiant Logistics (RLGT) +13% - Shares jumped after the logistics company reported strong FQ4 results with revenue rising 18.6% Y/Y. Adjusted net income increased 34.5% to $7.4M, while adjusted EBITDA rose 31.6% to $10.4M, and the adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 240 basis points to 15.5%. Gross profit increased 11.2% to $64.4M, with strength in U.S. forwarding operations and international airfreight. Radiant also amended its $200M revolving credit facility, extending maturity to 2031 and increasing its acquisition-focused accordion to $100M. The company entered fiscal 2027 with no net debt.

Biggest stock losers

  • Enova International (ENVA) -20% - Shares tumbled after the financial services company withdrew its applications with the OCC and Federal Reserve related to its proposed acquisition of Grasshopper Bancorp. Enova said the decision followed a thorough evaluation of the regulatory process, while CEO Steve Cunningham said the company did not believe regulatory guidelines provided clear standards for nonbanks seeking to become banks. The company reaffirmed its Q3 outlook for revenue growth of around 25% and adjusted EPS growth of around 30% Y/Y, along with FY2026 revenue growth of 20%-25% and adjusted EPS growth of 30%-35%. Enova also said it plans to accelerate share repurchases through the remainder of 2026, with $349M available under its current board authorization as of June 30.
  • Dave & Buster's Entertainment (PLAY) -14% - Shares plunged after higher food and beverage, payroll, and pre-opening costs pushed the entertainment and restaurant operator to an unexpected Q2 loss. Adjusted EPS came in at -$0.27, missing the $0.19 consensus and reversing from a $0.40 profit a year earlier, while adjusted EBITDA fell to $98.9M from $129.8M and missed the $118.8M estimate. Revenue declined 2.4% Y/Y, as comparable-store sales weakened and entertainment revenue declined. Food and beverage costs rose 11%, entertainment costs 5%, and payroll costs 1%, pushing total operating expenses up 4%.

  • Sysco (SYY) -2% - Shares fell after the foodservice distributor priced an offering of about 12.34M common shares at $81 each, with gross proceeds of roughly $1B. Sysco expects the offering to close September 16 and plans to use the net proceeds to finance part of the consideration for its pending acquisition of Jetro Restaurant Depot. Underwriters also have a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional $150M of shares at the same price to cover potential overallotments.
